headline: Our Lady of Victory monument to go to open bid for restoration; Taggart chosen to conserve Michael sculpture.
summary: Daedalus proposed taking Our Lady of Victory back to its original finish with three coats, while Taggart proposed a wash and one coat. The meeting gave the open call timeline as two to three months. The Taggart proposal for Michael lists $6,500 for cleaning and three coats. A community input form for Riverton Trolley Park is being prepared.
decisions: Approved taking the Our Lady of Victory conservation to the city's purchasing department for an open call for proposals.
Approved selecting Jonathan Taggart to perform conservation on Michael, 4-0 by roll call.
discussion: Our Lady of Victory restoration: Members compared the Daedalus and Taggart proposals. Daedalus would strip the statue to its original form and apply three coats, using scaffolding, while Taggart proposed one coat. Several views held that the longer-lasting work was worth the higher price.
Michael coating options: Members leaned toward the Taggart proposal, since the flat surface needs less detailed work. The proposal lists a $4,000 treatment and a $6,500 cleaning with three coats.
Riverton Trolley Park: Members visited the park and discussed public art there. They planned a community input form and sought five members for an artist selection panel.
Monument guidelines: Members are revising memorial and monument rules. Topics include who must approve a memorial for a person and how monuments differ from memorials.
Community art grant promotion: Members plan to rewrite the grant text and promote the grant more widely, after its funding increase.
